3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
4.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he commanded them' or 'he ordered them' — a single male instructing or directing a group to do something.
5.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action with a built-in third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The attached -hum is the object 'them' (a group of males), giving 'he commanded them'.

6.meaning: 'Their father' — the male parent belonging to a group. From a small set of nouns whose long final vowel shifts with case.
6.grammar: 'Father' is one of the special 'five nouns' that show case through a long vowel: the -ū here marks the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence. The attached -hum means 'their' (a group of males), so the whole is 'their father (as subject)'.

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

8.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

9.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'it avails, suffices, benefits, or makes free from need' — to be of use against something or to enrich and relieve someone of need. The root centres on richness, sufficiency, and being free of want.
9.grammar: An ongoing or future action. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the form (causative pattern) carries the sense of 'to make sufficient' or 'to be of avail'. The final long -ī is the verb's own weak-root termination.
9.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, sufficient

10.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
10.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

11.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
11.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
14.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

15.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
15.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

16.meaning: A need, want, or requirement — something one has need of, or a matter one wishes to fulfil.
16.grammar: A feminine noun (the -ah ending becomes -t- before the case vowel). The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a need') and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or, as often, to express a reason or circumstance ('out of a need').

17.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
17.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

18.meaning: Soul, self, inner being, or person — the living self of a being, the seat of desire and will; can also simply mean 'oneself'.
18.grammar: A feminine noun. The -i ending is genitive — the case typically used after a preposition or to link the word to a following noun in a possessive chain ('...of the soul / self'), as in 'the soul OF so-and-so'.

19.meaning: The proper name Yaʿqūb (the Prophet Jacob).
19.grammar: A proper name (a non-Arabic name treated as grammatically 'unable to take the full range of endings'). The -a ending marks it as an object or otherwise governed into the accusative; because such names are 'restricted', they take a single -a and do not add the 'n' (tanwīn) that ordinary nouns would.

20.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he carried it out', 'he fulfilled it', 'he decreed it', or 'he completed it' — a single male bringing some matter (feminine) to its conclusion or settling it.

parts.en: decreed / fulfilled / completed (3rd-person masculine singular past)

20.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action with a built-in third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The verb's third root letter is weak and surfaces as the long final -ā of the stem qaḍā (so the ending is absorbed into the stem, not a separate piece). The attached -hā is the object 'it/her' (referring to something grammatically feminine), giving 'he fulfilled it / carried it out'.
20.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, to settle, to fulfil, to complete

21.meaning: A linkage of 'and' with the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') plus 'he' — meaning 'and truly he…', opening a clause with firm assurance about the person referred to.
21.grammar: 'wa' is the connector 'and'. 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached -hu ('he/him') is the subject of the inna-clause, expressed in object form as inna requires.

22.meaning: An emphatic statement that someone is truly the holder or owner of something. The opening lām is a particle of emphasis ('surely/indeed'), and dhū means 'owner of, possessor of, the one endowed with' — it is a word that always governs a following noun to say someone is rich in or characterized by that thing.
22.grammar: The la- prefix is the 'lām of emphasis' that strengthens a statement ('indeed, surely'). Dhū is one of the special 'five nouns'; its long -ū ending marks the nominative (subject) case, the form used when this word is the doer or the thing being described, and it must be followed by a noun in the genitive ('possessor OF …').

23.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
23.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

24.meaning: To / for that which — a preposition 'to, for' joined to a relative word meaning 'what' or 'that which'.
24.grammar: A combination of the preposition li- ('to, for') with the relative pronoun mā ('that which'). Together they introduce something toward or for which an action is directed; mā itself does not change for case.

25.meaning: A past-tense verb 'We taught him' — to impart knowledge or skill thoroughly to a single male, with the act ascribed to a plural/majestic 'We'.
25.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. It is a Form II verb (intensified, 'to teach/instruct'). The -nā ending marks a first-person plural subject ('we'), which in divine speech expresses majesty. The attached -hu is the object 'him', giving 'We taught him'.
25.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; (Form II) to teach

26.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
26.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

27.meaning: 'More' / 'greater (in number or amount)' — the comparative/superlative form built from 'much, many', meaning more numerous or more abundant.
27.grammar: A comparative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('more …'). The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is an object or otherwise governed; this pattern does not take nunation. It is typically completed by 'than …'.

28.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
28.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
28.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

29.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
29.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

30.meaning: They know / they have knowledge — an ongoing or habitual knowing by a group.
30.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the third person; plurality is supplied by the -ūna ending, which together with the prefix gives 'they'. The full -ūna ending also marks the ordinary indicative mood — a plain statement of present or ongoing action.

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: A past-tense verb 'they entered' or 'they went in' — a plural group passing into a place or state.
2.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they', a group of males). The final silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending and is not pronounced.
2.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, to go in

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

4.meaning: Yusuf (Joseph) — the proper name of the prophet Joseph, son of Jacob. As a borrowed (non-Arabic) name it carries no Arabic root meaning; it functions simply as a personal name.
4.grammar: A proper noun (a person's name). The final -a ending is an accusative/oblique marker; because this name is grammatically 'diptote' (a class of names that refuse the normal -un/-in nunation), it takes a single -a in both the accusative and the genitive instead of the usual -i. So the -a typically signals that the name is either a direct object of a verb or the object of a preposition.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he took in', 'he sheltered', or 'he drew (someone) to himself' — a single male giving refuge or bringing another close to his side.

parts.en: sheltered / took in (Form IV verb stem)
weak final root-letter (3rd-person masculine singular past)

5.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action with a built-in third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). It is a Form IV verb ending in a weak vowel (the final root letter shown as the long -ā), meaning 'he gave shelter to' or 'he drew (someone) to himself'.
5.root: ا-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to take refuge, to give shelter

6.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

7.meaning: 'His brother' — a male sibling belonging to a single male. From the special set of nouns whose long final vowel changes with case.
7.grammar: 'Brother' is one of the special 'five nouns' that show case by a long vowel: the -ā here marks the accusative case — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('...his brother'). The attached -hu means 'his'.

8.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
8.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

9.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
9.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

10.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
10.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

11.meaning: 'Your brother' — a male sibling belonging to a single person addressed ('you'). From the special set of nouns whose long final vowel changes with case.
11.grammar: 'Brother' is one of the special 'five nouns' that show case by a long vowel: the -ū here marks the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence ('your brother'). The attached -ka means 'your' (addressing one male).

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
12.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

13.meaning: "You feel distressed / grieve / despair" — to be saddened, dejected or filled with misery over something.
13.grammar: A Form VIII (iftaʿala) present-tense verb of the 'feel misery' pattern. The ta- prefix marks 'you (singular)' or a feminine 'it/she' as the doer. Its vowelless ending (-is, jussive) is the form taken after particles like 'do not' or 'so', often giving a command or prohibition sense ('do not grieve').

14.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
14.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

15.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
15.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

16.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
16.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
16.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: "he equipped/provisioned them" — to fully outfit or supply someone, preparing and loading them with what they need.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of an intensive pattern (Form II, doubled middle consonant), which conveys thoroughness — fully outfitting or readying. The bare -a on the stem marks a completed action by a third-person masculine singular subject ("he did"). The attached -hum is the object "them."

3.meaning: "with their gear/provisions" — the equipment, supplies, or load that one is furnished with.
3.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition bi- ("with" / "by means of") and followed by the possessive pronoun -him ("their"). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive ending that the preposition requires; the pronoun then attaches to show ownership.

4.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'

5.meaning: A drinking-cup or vessel used for giving water to drink; also a watering-trough or the act of providing drink.
5.grammar: The definite article al- ('the') plus a noun of giving-to-drink (the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 's', shown by the doubling). The -a ending is accusative — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('...the drinking-cup').
5.root: س-ق-ي (s-q-y) — to give to drink, to water

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: A saddlebag, travelling-pack, or the load/baggage a traveller carries on a mount; by extension, a halting-place on a journey.
7.grammar: A masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive — the case typically used after a preposition or to link the word to a following noun in a possessive chain ('...of the bag', or 'the bag OF so-and-so').
7.root: ر-ح-ل (r-ḥ-l) — to journey, to load a mount for travel

8.meaning: 'His brother' — a male sibling, joined to the possessive 'his'. The word can also extend to a close kinsman, companion, or fellow within a shared group or bond.
8.grammar: The base word 'brother' here shows the long -ī linking vowel it takes when it is possessed and stands in the genitive (the 'of' / after-preposition form). The attached -hi means 'his'; its 'i' vowel harmonises with that preceding genitive form.

9.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
9.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

10.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he announced', 'he proclaimed', or 'he called out' — a single male making a loud public declaration so that others hear.
10.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action with a built-in third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). It is a Form II verb (intensified) from the root meaning 'to let know / give ear', so it conveys making a loud, public announcement or call.
10.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — ear; to give ear, to make known, to announce

11.meaning: An announcer / herald / proclaimer — one who makes a public call or proclamation, the active doer of announcing.
11.grammar: An active participle of the intensive (Form II) pattern, naming the one who performs the action ('one who announces'). The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('an announcer') and nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence.
11.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to give ear/listen; to announce/permit

12.meaning: A vocative phrase used to call out feminine or grammatically-feminine addressees — roughly 'O you (there)!', drawing the attention of the one being addressed.
12.grammar: A vocative ('calling') construction: the particle of address joined to 'ayyat-' with the pointing word -hā, used to summon a feminine noun that carries 'the'. The -u is the nominative ending standard on this vocative form. The whole functions as 'O you...!' addressing a feminine subject.

13.meaning: A caravan — a company of travellers and their pack-animals (such as camels) journeying together, especially carrying loads or trade.
13.grammar: The definite article al- ('the') plus the noun 'caravan'. The -u ending is nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for the one being addressed ('the caravan').
13.root: ع-ي-ر (ʿ-y-r) — caravan; pack-animals that come and go

14.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
14.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.

15.meaning: An emphatic statement that some people are indeed thieves — those who steal, who take by stealth what belongs to others. The opening 'la-' adds force, turning the claim into a strong assertion ('surely they are thieves').
15.grammar: An active participle ('one who does X') built on the pattern fāʿil, here meaning 'stealer/thief'. The prefixed 'la-' is the emphatic lām that strengthens a statement. The '-ūna' ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used for the subject or predicate ('they are …'); the alternative '-īna' would mark the accusative/genitive.

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: 'And they advanced / turned to face' — a past-tense report that a group came forward, approached, or directed themselves toward something. The verb conveys facing toward and drawing near, often with eager intent.

parts.en: to advance / turn toward (Form IV stem)

2.grammar: A Form IV past-tense verb (the a- prefix in 'aqbala' gives a sense of directing oneself toward). The '-ū' suffix is the masculine-plural subject marker meaning 'they (did it)'; the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention. The 'wa' is the connector 'and'.
2.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to face, come toward, accept

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
3.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
3.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: 'What…?' — a question word asking about a thing or matter, used to inquire 'what is it that…?' It is formed by joining 'what' with the demonstrative 'that.'
4.grammar: An interrogative compound made of mā ('what') plus dhā ('that'), together meaning 'what is it that…?' It is an indeclinable question word — it has no case ending and keeps one fixed form, introducing a question about a thing.

5.meaning: 'You (all) are missing / find lacking' — a present-tense verb describing the act of noticing that something is absent or lost, of failing to find what one expected to be there.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix together with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The final '-ūna' (with nūn) signals the indicative mood — the form used for ordinary, factual statements; dropping the nūn would mark the subjunctive or jussive.
5.root: ف-ق-د (f-q-d) — to lose, miss, find absent

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: 'We are missing / we find lacking' — a present-tense verb expressing that the speakers notice the absence of something and cannot find it.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we (do it).' The final '-u' marks the indicative mood, used for plain factual statements; a final '-a' would be subjunctive and a bare consonant (no vowel) would be jussive.
2.root: ف-ق-د (f-q-d) — to lose, miss, find absent

3.meaning: A drinking-cup, goblet, or measuring bowl — a vessel used for drinking and, in some usages, for measuring out grain.
3.grammar: A noun. The final '-a' is the accusative ending, the case typically used when the noun is the direct object of a verb ('we are looking for the cup'). The corresponding '-u' would mark the subject and '-i' the genitive.

4.meaning: 'The king' — a sovereign ruler who holds dominion and authority over a realm and its people.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the king'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, used when the word follows a preposition or is possessed by a preceding noun ('… OF the king'). The '-u' ending would mark the subject and '-a' the object.

5.meaning: 'And for whoever / and to the one who' — combining 'and,' the preposition 'for/to,' and the relative word 'man' meaning 'whoever' or 'the one who,' used of persons.
5.grammar: Three particles joined together. 'wa' is 'and'; 'li-' is the preposition 'for/to'; 'man' is a relative/conditional pronoun meaning 'whoever' or 'the one who,' used only for people (as opposed to 'mā' for things). These words do not take case endings.

6.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

7.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

8.meaning: A load or burden — the quantity of goods that is carried, especially a camel-load measured out as a reward or quantity of provision.
8.grammar: A noun. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being announced ('a load is …'). The '-a' ending would mark the object and '-i' the genitive.
8.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, bear, a load

9.meaning: A camel, or by extension the load a camel can carry — a camel-load as a unit of goods.
9.grammar: The -in ending is the indefinite genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of…' relationship to another noun, while the final -n (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite ('a camel('s load)').

10.meaning: 'And I' — the connector 'and' joined to the standalone first-person pronoun 'I.'
10.grammar: A connector plus an independent pronoun. 'wa' means 'and' (its consonant is doubled here by assimilation to the preceding word). 'anā' is the detached first-person singular pronoun 'I,' typically used to state or emphasize the subject. Independent pronouns do not change for case.

11.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
11.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

12.meaning: A guarantor or surety — one who takes responsibility and stands as a pledge that something will be delivered or fulfilled; also a spokesman or leader who answers for others.
12.grammar: A noun on the faʿīl pattern. The final '-un' is the nominative ending carrying tanwīn (the doubled 'n' sound that marks an indefinite noun, 'a guarantor'). Nominative is the case of the subject or predicate; the indefinite genitive would be '-in' and accusative '-an'.
12.root: ز-ع-م (z-ʿ-m) — to claim, vouch for, take charge

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: 'By Allah' — an oath-formula in which the particle 'ta-' attaches to the divine name to swear by Allah. The 'ta-' oath particle carries a nuance of surprise or emphatic insistence.
2.grammar: An oath construction. The prefixed 'ta-' is an oath particle ('by …'), a less common variant of the more usual 'wa-' / 'bi-' oaths and reserved almost entirely for the name of Allah. Words after an oath particle take the genitive case, shown here by the final '-i'.

3.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
3.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

4.meaning: 'You (all) have known / you knew' — a past-tense verb stating that a group came to know, recognized, or were aware of something.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-tum' is the attached subject pronoun for second-person masculine plural ('you all did it'). In the past tense the doer is shown by such endings rather than by a prefix.

5.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
5.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

6.meaning: We came / We brought — to arrive, or to bring something forward and present it.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-nā' is the subject ending meaning 'we (did it),' marking a completed action performed by a first-person plural — something already brought about.

7.meaning: 'So that we cause corruption / spread mischief' — a verb expressing the act of ruining, spoiling, or working harm and disorder in the land. The leading 'li-' frames it as a purpose ('in order to corrupt').
7.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb meaning 'to spread corruption.' The 'nu-' prefix means 'we'; the prefix vowel 'u' is characteristic of Form IV. The leading 'li-' is the particle of purpose ('so that'), and it puts the verb into the subjunctive mood, shown by the final '-a' (instead of the indicative '-u').
7.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — to be corrupt, spoil, cause disorder

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
11.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

12.meaning: 'Thieves' — those who steal, who take by stealth what is not theirs.
12.grammar: An active participle ('one who steals') on the fāʿil pattern, here plural. The '-īna' ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — the form used for objects, after prepositions, or as the predicate of certain verbs; the alternative '-ūna' would mark the nominative.

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
2.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

3.meaning: 'Its recompense / its requital' — the repayment, penalty, or due return for a deed, with an attached pronoun 'it/his' indicating whose or of-what the recompense is.
3.grammar: A noun ('recompense') with an attached possessive pronoun '-hu' ('its/his'). The case vowel '-u' before the pronoun is nominative, marking the word as the subject or the thing being announced ('its recompense is …'). The attached '-hu' serves as a possessor ('… of it').

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
5.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

6.meaning: 'Liars / ones who lie' — people characterised by speaking falsehood.
6.grammar: An active participle ('one who lies') on the 'fāʿil' pattern, in the sound masculine plural. The '-īna' ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case — the form used when the word is an object or otherwise not the subject.
6.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — lying, falsehood, denying the truth

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: 'Its recompense / its requital' — the repayment, penalty, or due return for a deed, with an attached pronoun 'it/his' indicating whose or of-what the recompense is.
2.grammar: A noun ('recompense') with an attached possessive pronoun '-hu' ('its/his'). The case vowel '-u' before the pronoun is nominative, marking the word as the subject or the thing being announced ('its recompense is …'). The attached '-hu' serves as a possessor ('… of it').

3.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
3.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

4.meaning: 'It was found / it is found' — a passive past-tense verb stating that something was discovered or came to be located, with no mention of who did the finding.

parts.en: stem vowel (3rd masc. sing., zero-marked subject)

4.grammar: A passive past-tense verb. The internal vowel pattern 'u–i' (wujida) marks it as passive, so the meaning is 'it was found' rather than 'he found.' The final '-a' is the inherent stem vowel of the past-tense pattern, not a person/number suffix; the third-person masculine singular ('it') is the unmarked, default form and carries no overt subject ending (compare the marked endings '-tu' for 'I,' '-nā' for 'we,' '-tum' for 'you all'). The doubled 'w' at the start is assimilation to a preceding word.
4.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, exist

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'His saddlebag / his pack' — the travelling-bag or load-pack of a rider, with an attached pronoun meaning 'his.'
6.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive '-hi' ('his'). The case vowel '-i' is genitive, the case used after prepositions or when the noun is possessed; the pronoun takes the form '-hi' (rather than '-hu') precisely because it follows this '-i' vowel.

7.meaning: A two-part phrase: the connector 'then / so' plus the standalone pronoun 'he / it,' used to point back and resume with 'then he…' or 'so it…'
7.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') plus the detached subject pronoun 'huwa' ('he/it'), 3rd-person masculine singular. Both are indeclinable, with no case ending; the pronoun typically begins or emphasizes a statement about 'he/it.'

8.meaning: 'Its recompense / its requital' — the repayment, penalty, or due return for a deed, with an attached pronoun 'it/his' indicating whose or of-what the recompense is.
8.grammar: A noun ('recompense') with an attached possessive pronoun '-hu' ('its/his'). The case vowel '-u' before the pronoun is nominative, marking the word as the subject or the thing being announced ('its recompense is …'). The attached '-hu' serves as a possessor ('… of it').

9.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
9.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
9.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

10.meaning: 'We reward / We requite' — to repay or recompense someone for their deeds, whether with good or with due consequence.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we'. The stem ends in a long '-ī' (a weak final root letter); in the plain indicative this final '-ī' is what is heard, giving 'we reward'.
10.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to repay, to recompense, to requite

11.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
11.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: 'So he began / made a start' — a past-tense verb marking the commencement of an action, often introducing what someone set about doing. The leading 'fa-' means 'so/then.'

parts.en: stem vowel (3rd masc. sing., zero-marked subject)

1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The final '-a' is the inherent stem vowel of the Form I past pattern (faʿala), not a subject suffix; the third-person masculine singular ('he') is the default, unmarked form and takes no overt subject ending (unlike the marked endings '-tu' for 'I,' '-ta/-ti' for 'you,' '-nā' for 'we'). The prefixed 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then,' often signalling sequence or consequence.

2.meaning: 'With their containers / their sacks' — combining the preposition 'with/by' and the plural noun 'containers' (vessels or bags that hold things), plus 'their.'

parts.en: the tāʾ marbūṭa pronounced as 't' before a suffix + genitive ending

2.grammar: A preposition plus a plural noun with an attached possessive: bi-awʿiyati-him. 'bi-' means 'with/by.' 'awʿiya' is a broken (internal) plural of wiʿāʾ, 'container'; its feminine-plural ending is written with tāʾ marbūṭa (ة), which is silent in isolation but sounded as a full 't' once a suffix is attached — hence the stem appears as 'awʿiyat-' here. The case vowel '-i' on that 't' is genitive, required after the preposition 'bi-,' and the pronoun appears as '-him' ('their') in harmony with that '-i' vowel.

3.meaning: An adverb of time and place meaning 'before' — denoting what comes prior to something else, whether earlier in time or ahead of it in sequence.
3.grammar: An adverb of time/place ending in -a. It is regularly placed before a following noun to mean 'before that thing' (e.g. 'before X'), functioning much like a preposition that the next word completes.
3.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, to come before; the front/fore

4.meaning: A container, vessel, or sack — anything that holds or stores something inside it.
4.grammar: A noun. The final '-i' is the genitive ending, used after a preposition or when the word is possessed by a following noun ('the container OF …'). The '-u' ending would mark the subject and '-a' the object.

5.meaning: 'His brother' — a male sibling, joined to the possessive 'his'. The word can also extend to a close kinsman, companion, or fellow within a shared group or bond.
5.grammar: The base word 'brother' here shows the long -ī linking vowel it takes when it is possessed and stands in the genitive (the 'of' / after-preposition form). The attached -hi means 'his'; its 'i' vowel harmonises with that preceding genitive form.

6.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
6.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

7.meaning: 'He brought it out / extracted it' — a past-tense verb for drawing or pulling something out from where it was, with an attached object pronoun 'it' (feminine).

parts.en: to bring out, extract (Form X stem)
stem vowel (3rd masc. sing., zero-marked subject)

7.grammar: A Form X past-tense verb (the 'ista-' prefix often conveys seeking or drawing something out). The '-a' is the base vowel of the Form X past stem (istafʿala), not a subject suffix; the third-person masculine singular ('he') is the default, unmarked form with no overt subject ending. The attached '-hā' is the object pronoun 'it/her,' naming what was brought out.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: A container, vessel, or sack — anything that holds or stores something inside it.
9.grammar: A noun. The final '-i' is the genitive ending, used after a preposition or when the word is possessed by a following noun ('the container OF …'). The doubled 'w' at the start is assimilation to a preceding word; the '-u' ending would mark the subject and '-a' the object.

10.meaning: 'His brother' — a male sibling, joined to the possessive 'his'. The word can also extend to a close kinsman, companion, or fellow within a shared group or bond.
10.grammar: The base word 'brother' here shows the long -ī linking vowel it takes when it is possessed and stands in the genitive (the 'of' / after-preposition form). The attached -hi means 'his'; its 'i' vowel harmonises with that preceding genitive form.

11.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
11.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
11.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

12.meaning: 'We devised / planned / contrived' — a past-tense verb describing the arranging of a subtle scheme or stratagem to bring about an outcome.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb whose middle root-letter is a weak 'y' that drops out, leaving the short stem 'kid-.' The suffix '-nā' is the attached subject pronoun 'we (did it).' In the past tense the doer is shown by such endings rather than a prefix.
12.root: ك-ي-د (k-y-d) — to scheme, plot, contrive a stratagem

13.meaning: For/to Yūsuf — the proper name Joseph, with the preposition "to/for" attached.
13.grammar: A proper name (of non-Arabic origin) preceded by the preposition li- ("to/for"). As a "diptote" name it resists full inflection, so even in the genitive (required after li-) it takes -a instead of the usual -i, and never takes tanwīn.

14.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
14.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

15.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

15.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

16.meaning: 'So that he may take / in order to seize' — a verb of taking, grasping, or seizing, framed by the leading 'li-' as the purpose ('in order to take').
16.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix marks the third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The leading 'li-' is the particle of purpose ('so that'), which puts the verb into the subjunctive mood, shown by the final '-a' (instead of the indicative '-u').

17.meaning: 'His brother' — a male sibling belonging to a single male. From the special set of nouns whose long final vowel changes with case.
17.grammar: 'Brother' is one of the special 'five nouns' that show case by a long vowel: the -ā here marks the accusative case — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('...his brother'). The attached -hu means 'his'.

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
18.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

19.meaning: 'Religion, way of life, creed' — but also the broad sense of a binding system one lives by, the recompense one is owed, and submission/obedience to a higher authority. It denotes a complete way of devotion and accountability, not merely a set of beliefs.
19.grammar: A noun. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition or possessive construction.

20.meaning: 'The king' — a sovereign ruler who holds dominion and authority over a realm and its people.
20.grammar: A definite noun ('the king'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, used when the word follows a preposition or is possessed by a preceding noun ('… OF the king'). The '-u' ending would mark the subject and '-a' the object.

21.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
21.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

22.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
22.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

23.meaning: '(that) he wills / wishes' — to will, intend, or so desire that a thing comes about.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he wills'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that/so that/until,' giving the sense 'that he should will.'

24.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
24.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

25.meaning: 'We raise / We lift up' — to elevate something or someone in rank, degree, or standing; ongoing or repeated action.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we', and the '-u' ending marks the plain indicative (an ongoing or habitual 'we raise / we keep raising').
25.root: ر-ف-ع (r-f-ʿ) — to raise, to lift, to elevate

26.meaning: "degrees / ranks / levels / steps" — the plural of daraja, a step or grade in an ascending scale; it denotes ranks, levels, or stages of elevation.
26.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -in (with nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('degrees, ranks') and in the accusative/genitive case — the form used as an object or after a preposition.
26.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — step, grade, to ascend by degrees

27.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
27.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

28.meaning: 'We will / We wish' — to will, want, or choose for something to be; expresses volition.
28.grammar: A present-tense verb. The prefix means 'we'; the '-u' ending marks the plain indicative ('we will / we wish'). Its nūn carries a shadda (doubling) because the preceding connector 'man' ('whoever') merges into it, so it is sounded '-nn-'.
28.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to want

29.meaning: A combination of the connector 'and/but' with the noun meaning 'above, over, on top of'. As a noun it denotes a position higher than something else; figuratively it can mean 'beyond' or 'superior to'.
29.grammar: The opening 'wa' is a joining particle ('and', sometimes contrastive 'but'). 'Fawqa' is an adverb of place fixed in the accusative-shaped -a ending, functioning as 'above/over' and typically governing a following noun in the genitive ('above … of …').

30.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
30.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

31.meaning: Possessor of / the one having — a relational word meaning 'owner of' or 'endowed with,' used to attach a quality or relationship to the noun it describes.
31.grammar: A relational noun meaning 'owner/possessor of,' which must be followed by another noun ('possessor OF …'). It declines for case: dhū (nominative), dhī (genitive), dhā (accusative). The form dhī (ending -ī) is its genitive, used when it follows a preposition or describes a preceding genitive noun. It never stands alone; it always governs a following noun.
31.root: — (a relational noun meaning 'possessor of'; no verbal root)

32.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
32.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

33.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
33.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
2.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

3.meaning: An action-verb meaning 'he steals / he commits theft' — to take what belongs to another secretly and wrongfully.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), shown by the ya- prefix. The prefix carries a shadda (doubling) because the yā has assimilated a preceding particle, so it is written 'yya-'. The bare, vowel-less final consonant (-q with sukūn) is the jussive/clipped mood, the form used after conditional and negating particles, giving the sense 'if/should he steal' or 'let him not steal'.

4.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
4.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

5.meaning: A completed-action verb: 'he stole', he carried out a theft in the past.
5.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), built on the basic pattern faʿala. The final -a vowel is the standard ending of this past-tense form; the act is presented as finished.

6.meaning: A brother — a male sibling; by extension a close kinsman, comrade, or member of the same group. The final nunation (-un) marks it as a singular, indefinite noun ('a brother').
6.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, marking it as the doer/subject or the thing being named, and corresponds to English 'a brother'.

7.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
7.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
9.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
9.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

10.meaning: A cluster meaning roughly 'so/then he kept it hidden': the linking word 'so/then', plus a verb 'he kept secret / concealed within himself', plus an attached 'it/her'.
10.grammar: Opens with 'fa' ('so, then', marking sequence or result). The verb is past-tense, third-person masculine singular, in the causative/transitivizing Form IV (afʿala) pattern, here 'asarra meaning 'to keep hidden, conceal inwardly' (the doubled rā reflects the geminate root س-ر-ر). The attached 'hā' is an object pronoun, 'it/her', receiving the action.

11.meaning: Yūsuf (Joseph), the proper name of the Prophet. A non-Arabic personal name.
11.grammar: A proper name that is diptote (it does not take tanwīn and resists the normal -i for genitive). The final -u is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the one being named/spoken about.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: 'Himself; his own self/soul' — the inner self, soul, or person of a male individual; used reflexively to point back to the person himself.
13.grammar: The noun 'nafs' ('self/soul') with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically follows a preposition or links the noun possessively to what precedes ('the self OF him' = 'himself'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this preceding '-i' vowel; the long vowel mark indicates it is pronounced '-hī'.

14.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
14.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'he discloses / brings to light / makes it appear', with an attached 'it/her' — to reveal something previously hidden.
15.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the causative Form IV pattern (afʿala), here 'abdā 'to make appear, reveal'. The weak final letter is dropped to a clipped form (jussive), the shape used after conditional or negating words. The attached 'hā' is the object, 'it/her'.

16.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
16.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

17.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
17.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

18.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
18.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

19.meaning: Evil, bad, or harmful — that which is wicked or detrimental; can also mean 'worse' in comparison.
19.grammar: A noun (also used as a comparative, 'worse'). The ending -un is the nominative with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking an indefinite noun, 'a …'). The nominative generally marks the word as the subject or as the thing being described.

20.meaning: 'A place, position, or station' — a noun for a location or standing where something or someone is situated, literally or figuratively (rank, status).
20.grammar: A noun. The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a place') and accusative — a case often used to specify in what respect something holds true ('… in position/place'), as well as for direct objects.
20.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come to be, existence (place of being)

21.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
21.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
21.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

22.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
22.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

23.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
23.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

24.meaning: 'You describe / you allege / you ascribe' — an ongoing or repeated act, by a group, of characterizing something, stating what it is like, or putting forward a claim about it. Waṣafa means to describe, depict, or attribute a quality.
24.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person ('you') subject, and the ending -ūna marks a masculine plural with continuing or habitual action — so 'you (all) describe/allege.' The retained -na ending shows the verb is in its plain (indicative) mood.
24.root: و-ص-ف (w-ṣ-f) — describing, depicting, attributing a quality

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
2.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

3.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
3.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

4.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
4.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

5.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
5.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

6.meaning: The noun 'father' — a male parent; by extension a forefather or one who stands in a father's place.
6.grammar: A singular noun, indefinite ('a father'), in the accusative case shown by the -an ending (the double-fatḥa tanwīn). The accusative typically marks a direct object or the noun named after certain particles.

7.meaning: An old man; one aged, an elder. The noun denotes a man advanced in years (and by extension a venerable elder or chief).
7.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite ('an old man') and in the accusative case — the case often used to specify a state or condition (e.g. 'being an old man').
7.root: ش-ي-خ (sh-y-kh) — old age, an elder or aged man

8.meaning: Large, great, big, or major — an adjective describing something of great size, amount, or importance. It can also mean elder/older in age. The -an ending leaves it indefinite ('a large …').
8.grammar: An indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn): it commonly marks the object of a verb, or works adverbially, and signals the word is indefinite ('a large one'). It pairs with ṣaghīr ('small').
8.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, largeness, being great or old

9.meaning: An imperative meaning 'take!', 'seize!', or 'take hold of!', addressed to a single male, with the attached 'fa-' meaning 'so' or 'then'.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) to one male person ('you'), with the 'you (masc. sing.)' built into the form. 'fa-' is a connecting particle expressing sequence or consequence ('so', 'then').
9.root: ا-خ-ذ / ء-خ-ذ (’-kh-dh) — to take, seize, take hold of

10.meaning: A combination of 'one (of), a single one' plus 'us' — i.e. 'one of us', a single individual belonging to our group.
10.grammar: The noun 'aḥad ('one, a single one') carries the accusative -a ending (object or specified noun), and is joined to the attached pronoun 'nā' ('us'), which puts it in a possessive/partitive relation, 'one of us'.

11.meaning: 'Its place' or 'its location' — the spot or position belonging to it.
11.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hu' ('its / his'). The '-a' ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb or an adverb of place ('in its place').

12.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
12.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

13.meaning: 'We see you' — to perceive or regard you, whether with the eyes or in the sense of considering/judging you to be a certain way.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb from a 'weak' root whose final letter drops. The 'na-' prefix means 'we', and the attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (one male). Together: 'we see / we regard you'.
13.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — seeing, perceiving, forming an opinion

14.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
14.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

15.meaning: 'The doers of good / those who act with excellence and beauty'. It denotes people who do what is good and do it well — acting righteously, generously, and with sincerity, as if conscious of being watched by Allah.

parts.en: good-doers / those who excel in doing good

15.grammar: A definite plural active participle (the 'doer' form of the verb 'to do good'). The prefixed al- means 'the'. The ending -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the object/oblique state — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. It refers to male (or mixed) persons characterized by the action.
15.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful; to do well and excellently

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: Seeking of refuge — a noun expressing taking shelter and protection; idiomatically "I seek refuge (in Allah)!" as an exclamation of recoiling from wrong.
2.grammar: A verbal noun naming the act of taking refuge, used in an exclamatory, emphatic way. The -a ending is accusative; in this idiom it is the accusative of a noun set down as an absolute statement ("refuge [I seek]!"), and it is then linked to a following word naming the one in whom refuge is sought.

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
